tasks.title: Process confinement on Linux and macOS: contained tier from Cua, Safe registered-exec parity
tasks.objective: Registered-executable Safe execution with owned process-tree cleanup and resource bounds on Linux and macOS, matching what Job Objects/AppContainer give on Windows.
tasks.user_visible: process_spawn works on macOS and Linux with the same bounds.
tasks.dependencies: Inside apps/orcel-contain only: tokio (as the donor uses it), libc, and the windows-sys features the donor's windows.rs needs, admitted with cargo-deny and cargo-audit on that workspace. Kernel side: std only.
steps: Create apps/orcel-contain as its own Cargo workspace (like apps/orcel-native-host), by COPY_ADAPT of Cua's perception containment (MIT). The donor code uses tokio (containment.rs AsyncReadExt and tokio::time::timeout; linux.rs tokio::process ChildStdin/ChildStdout), so it stays async inside this helper and tokio never enters the kernel's 62-package lockfile (AD-16). Keep the capability-reporting contract (refuse to spawn when any advertised boundary cannot be installed): Linux Landlock + seccomp + rlimits + PDEATHSIG + NO_NEW_PRIVS, macOS Seatbelt + rlimits + sentinel, Windows AppContainer + Job Object + private desktop. The helper is a one-shot launcher: orceld (or the browser host) passes a closed, bounded spec over stdin (executable, argv, read/write allowlist, limits), the helper installs every boundary, runs the child, relays bounded stdout/stderr and exit status, and exits. No listener.

crates/orcel-provider-process/src/contained.rs is the kernel-side client of that helper (std only): it pins the helper binary, writes the spec and reads a bounded result. The 'contained' tier (no network, exact read/write allowlist, no fork) serves parsers and helpers (WI-05) and is an opt-in tier for registered executables.

Safe registered-executable parity on Linux/macOS (needs fork and sometimes network, so it cannot use the contained tier): process group, PR_SET_PDEATHSIG, pidfd (Linux) or kqueue EVFILT_PROC (macOS), rlimits, cgroup v2 child when delegated; kill the group on drop. This glue is BUILD_NEW but reuses unix.rs helpers from the copied crate.
Same registered-executable rules and output bounds; SG-000096 shell semantics are not ported here.

Packaging: the helper ships with Orcel on every OS and is resolved only from the signed install root by a pinned path (no PATH lookup), verified like the native host before launch. XP-16 (macOS bundle), XP-17 (Linux packages) and the Windows lifecycle payload (SG-000106) include it.
